messages.subject: Graphs from Class(Predict)
parts:
Frank Harrell's rms package is exquisite, as many know. The default
graphics are eloquent. However, they are lattice based, and trying to
tweak them is a bit tricky for someone who has had the benefit of only
ever using ggplot! Given Hadley's recent talks at Vanderbuilt, and
explicit mentions in the newly released rms package, I suspect we are
going to see greater integration of rms and ggplot in the future. This
would be most welcome.

So, and this is probably more an R question than a ggplot question, but
has anyone tried to turn Class(Predict) objects into
data frames for manipulation under ggplot? I'll worry about the ggplot
syntax once I have a data frame.


Here's my situation:

I am trying to generate a faceted heat-map, arising from the following
Predict statement:

pm13 <-Predict(model8, digitaltime, rnadlerbv, rexactage=c(17, 20, 25,
30, 40, 50, 60), DW_firsttime =" (1)first time", fun=plogis)

messages.subject: Re: Graphs from Class(Predict)
parts:
Answering my own question... it turns out this was easier and more
direct then I expected to integrate Predict class objects and ggplot.

The output of Predict has two concurrent classes: Predict and dataframe,
and the dataframe class can be fed directly into ggplot.


R


> str(pm14)

Classes ‘Predict’ and 'data.frame': 80000 obs. of 13 variables:
$ rnadlerbv : num 2610 2644 2678 2713 2747 ...

.. ..- attr(*, "names")= chr "rnadlerbv" "rexactage" "DW_firsttime"
"digitaltime" ...
..$ dimnames:List of 10

"rnadlerbv=2678" "rnadlerbv=2713" ...

.. ..$ rexactage : chr "rexactage=17.00" "rexactage=17.27"
"rexactage=17.53" "rexactage=17.80" ...

(1)first time"
